courses.title: C Programming
courses.description: Master procedural programming, pointers, memory allocation, and foundational algorithmic thinking.

lessons.title: C Syntax, Compilers & Structure
lessons.summary: Understanding main(), header files, compilation pipeline (preprocessor -> assembler -> linker).

lessons.title: Variables, Constants & Data Types
lessons.summary: Primitive types, format specifiers (%d, %f, %c), variable declarations and memory limits.

lessons.title: Conditional Statements (if-else, switch)
lessons.summary: Branching constructs, ternary operators, nested conditions, and efficient switch fall-through.

lessons.title: For, While & Do-While Loops
lessons.summary: Iteration logic, infinite loops prevention, break, continue, and loop invariant patterns.

lessons.title: Function Prototypes & Call by Value
lessons.summary: Function signatures, parameter passing, stack frames, and recursive function bases.

lessons.title: Recursion & Call Stack Dynamics
lessons.summary: Base cases, recursion depth, stack overflow diagnostics, and memoization concepts.

lessons.title: Understanding Memory Addresses & Dereferencing
lessons.summary: The & and * operators, pointer arithmetic, void pointers, and segfault debugging.

lessons.title: Dynamic Memory: malloc, calloc, realloc & free
lessons.summary: Heap allocation lifecycle, memory leaks prevention, dangling pointer traps.

lessons.title: User Defined Data Types: struct & typedef
lessons.summary: Grouping heterogeneous records, alignment, padding, and nested structs.

lessons.title: File Operations (fopen, fread, fwrite, fclose)
lessons.summary: Text vs binary streams, file pointers, error checking with feof and ferror.

courses.title: C++ Object-Oriented Programming
courses.description: Dive into Classes, Objects, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Standard Template Library (STL).

courses.title: Java Core & Enterprise
courses.description: Master Java OOP, Collections Framework, Streams API, Multithreading, and JDBC fundamentals.

courses.title: Python Fundamentals & Scripting
courses.description: Learn clean Python syntax, list comprehensions, file handling, and introductory data science packages.

lessons.title: Python Variables, Constants & Data Types
lessons.summary: Dynamic typing, numeric types, strings, standard input/output, and type casting in Python.

lessons.title: Conditions & Logical Branching
lessons.summary: Boolean logic, if-elif-else statements, identity and membership operators.

lessons.title: Python Loops for Beginners
lessons.summary: For loops, while loops, range() sequences, loop control statements, and iteration patterns.

lessons.title: Functions & Scope Dynamics
lessons.summary: Def signatures, positional vs keyword arguments, default values, return values, and global/local scope.

courses.title: HTML & CSS Responsive Design
courses.description: Build beautiful, accessible, mobile-first responsive interfaces using modern HTML5 and Vanilla CSS.

lessons.title: Semantic Tags: header, main, nav, section, article
lessons.summary: Accessible document outline, ARIA landmark roles, SEO optimization.

lessons.title: Forms, Validations & Input Types
lessons.summary: Native input attributes (pattern, required), accessible labels, fieldsets.

lessons.title: Flexbox Deep Dive: Axes, Alignment & Wrapping
lessons.summary: Main-axis vs cross-axis, justify-content, align-items, flex-grow/shrink dynamics.

lessons.title: CSS Grid: Templates, Areas & Minmax

courses.title: JavaScript Modern ES6+ & Async
courses.description: Master modern ECMAScript, closures, the event loop, Promises, Fetch API, and DOM manipulation.

lessons.title: Arrow Functions, Destructuring & Rest/Spread
lessons.summary: Lexical this binding, object/array destructuring patterns, rest parameters.

lessons.title: Scope, Closures & Execution Contexts
lessons.summary: Lexical environment, closures for private data encapsulation, memory retention.

lessons.title: Event Loop, Microtasks & Macrotasks
lessons.summary: Call stack, Web APIs, microtask queue (Promises) vs task queue (setTimeout).

lessons.title: Promises & Async/Await Error Handling

courses.title: SQL Database Design & Queries

courses.title: Data Structures & Algorithms

courses.title: Full-Stack Web Development

questions.question: Which loop construct in C is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop evaluates its condition at the end of the iteration, guaranteeing that the body executes at least once before the check.

questions.question: What is the output of `for(int i = 0; i < 5; i += 2) { printf("%d ", i); }` in C?
questions.explanation: i starts at 0, prints 0, becomes 2, prints 2, becomes 4, prints 4, then becomes 6 and stops because 6 < 5 is false.

questions.question: In C, if `int arr[5] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};`, what is the value of `*(arr + 2)`?
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic: `arr` points to index 0. `arr + 2` points to index 2, and dereferencing `*(arr + 2)` yields the value 30.

questions.question: What happens if you access `arr[10]` in an array declared as `int arr[5]` in standard C?
questions.explanation: C does not perform bounds checking on array indices. Accessing beyond the boundary invokes undefined behavior and can cause segmentation faults.

questions.question: What is the mechanism used by default when passing parameters to functions in C?
questions.explanation: C strictly uses Call by Value. Passing pointers passes the value of the memory address, not a native reference.

questions.question: What is the result of returning the address of a local automatic variable from a C function?
options: Dangling pointer leading to undefined behavior
questions.explanation: Automatic local variables are deallocated when the function's stack frame pops. Returning their address produces a dangling pointer.

questions.question: If `int *ptr = NULL;`, what occurs when attempting `*ptr = 100;` on modern protected memory operating systems?
questions.explanation: Dereferencing a NULL pointer triggers a hardware memory protection fault, resulting in immediate program termination (SIGSEGV).

questions.question: Which operator is used to obtain the memory address of an existing variable in C?
questions.explanation: The unary `&` (address-of) operator retrieves the memory address of its operand.

questions.question: Which CSS property aligns flex items along the primary (main) axis?
questions.explanation: `justify-content` defines how remaining space is distributed between and around flex items along the main axis.

questions.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr));` achieve?
options: A responsive layout that automatically fits as many 250px+ columns as possible without media queries
Stretches a single item to fill 250px
questions.explanation: This classic modern CSS pattern creates an inherently responsive grid that wraps columns automatically when screen width changes.

questions.question: Where do resolved Promise callbacks (`.then()`) execute in the JavaScript runtime?
options: Directly on the Call Stack synchronously
questions.explanation: Promises use the Microtask queue, which has higher priority than the Macrotask queue and drains completely before the next render or timer.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be re-assigned in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: `const` creates a block-scoped constant reference that prevents reassignment.

questions.explanation: Base case terminates recursive calls.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each step, giving logarithmic time complexity.

questions.explanation: do-while evaluates the loop guard condition after executing the body, ensuring at least one pass.

questions.question: What is the value printed by this code: int a = 5; int *p = &a; printf("%d", *p + 2);?
questions.explanation: *p dereferences a (5), and 5 + 2 evaluates to 7.

questions.question: What happens when a function attempts to return the address of a local automatic variable allocated on the stack frame?
options: Dangling pointer leading to undefined behavior
Automatic promotion to static heap memory
questions.correctAnswer: Dangling pointer leading to undefined behavior
questions.explanation: Stack frames are deallocated upon return; references to local automatic variables become dangling pointers.

library_ebooks.title: C Programming Complete Guide
library_ebooks.author: Prof. K. Ramanujan
library_ebooks.subject: C Programming
library_ebooks.description: Comprehensive textbook covering fundamentals from primitive data structures and memory allocation to advanced pointer manipulation.
library_ebooks.contentSnippet:
CHAPTER 1: C PROGRAMMING ARCHITECTURE
C is a procedural programming language designed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs. It provides low-level memory access via pointers while retaining structured programming semantics.

CHAPTER 2: VARIABLES & MEMORY LAYOUT
A variable is a named storage location. In C, integers typically take 4 bytes, chars 1 byte, and pointers 8 bytes on 64-bit systems.

CHAPTER 3: CONTROL FLOW & LOOPS
for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) allows deterministic iterative execution. while() checks conditions beforehand, while do-while() guarantees at least one execution.

CHAPTER 4: POINTER ARITHMETIC
A pointer stores the address of a memory block. & retrieves an address, * dereferences it to read or write the underlying value.

library_ebooks.title: Python 3: From Scripting to Systems
library_ebooks.author: Dr. Sunita Rao
library_ebooks.subject: Python
library_ebooks.description: Practical engineering handbook on Python scripting, generator expressions, object-oriented design, and standard library tools.
library_ebooks.contentSnippet:
MODULE 1: PYTHON DYNAMICS
Python is an interpreted, high-level, dynamically typed language emphasizing readable syntax and DRY architecture.

MODULE 2: FUNCTIONS & FIRST-CLASS OBJECTS
Functions in Python are first-class citizens. They can be passed as arguments, assigned to variables, and returned from other functions.

MODULE 3: LIST COMPREHENSIONS & GENERATORS
Generators allow lazy evaluation, consuming memory proportional to the current element rather than the entire collection.

library_ebooks.title: Algorithms & Data Structures in Practice
library_ebooks.author: CSE Faculty Circle
library_ebooks.subject: Data Structures
library_ebooks.description: Rigorous yet readable guide on asymptotic analysis, balanced search trees, graph traversal algorithms, and dynamic programming.
library_ebooks.contentSnippet:
SECTION 1: ASYMPTOTIC COMPLEXITY
Big-O defines the upper bound of algorithm runtime growth. Logarithmic O(log n) scaling separates feasible systems from intractable calculations.

SECTION 2: LINEAR STRUCTURES
Stacks operate on Last-In First-Out (LIFO); Queues operate on First-In First-Out (FIFO). Both admit O(1) push and pop operations.

SECTION 3: TREES & HEAPS
Binary Search Trees maintain ordered keys, yielding average O(log n) search, insert, and delete performance.

library_ebooks.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
library_ebooks.author: Academic Board
library_ebooks.subject: AI & ML
library_ebooks.description: Accessible introduction to state space search, heuristic evaluation, perceptrons, backpropagation, and practical model validation.
library_ebooks.contentSnippet:
CHAPTER 1: THE INTELLIGENT AGENT PARADIGM
Agents perceive their environment through sensors and act upon it via actuators. Rational agents strive to maximize expected performance metrics.

CHAPTER 2: SEARCH & OPTIMIZATION
A* search combines path cost g(n) with admissible heuristic h(n) to guarantee optimal paths on graphs.

CHAPTER 3: SUPERVISED LEARNING & GRADIENT DESCENT
Linear models adjust weight vectors along the negative gradient of the loss surface, converging toward minimal empirical error.
